overall: AG found five e-mails and memoranda sent by Selectman Simon to fellow members were individual Open Meeting Law violations, not Board-wide violations; ordered compliance and release of the referenced e-mails within 30 days.

allegations.summary: Board argued some complaints were untimely because the e-mails were public records reasonably discoverable when sent; AG found the complaints timely.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore conclude that the e-mails were not reasonably discoverable at the time they were sent.

allegations.summary: Aug. 20, 2013 memorandum by a selectman to other members, offering opinions and motions, allegedly deliberated outside an open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore conclude that the circulation of the August 20, 2013 memorandum also constituted improper deliberation.

allegations.summary: Oct. 2013 e-mail to board members on alcohol regulations, with the selectman's suggested changes, allegedly deliberated outside an open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The October 12, 2013 e-mail concerning the alcohol regulations addressed whether to adopt changes to Town policy.

allegations.summary: Jan. 2014 e-mail from a selectman to the Community Preservation Committee, copied to all board members, on BFRT funding allegedly deliberated outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The January 16, 2014 e-mail contained Selectman Simon's opinion regarding appropriate levels of funding for the BFRT.

allegations.summary: Aug. 4, 2014 memorandum on the BFRT circulated by e-mail to board members, placed in meeting packets, allegedly deliberated outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, the August 4, 2014 memorandum contained multiple opinions on topics within the Board's jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Aug. 19, 2014 reply by a selectman to all members about a proposed restaurant; board argued it was merely a social issue outside its jurisdiction. AG found an individual violation, not a Board violation.
allegations.key_passage: Because issues relating to a new restaurant opening in town could conceivably come before the Board, we find that this discussion was within the Board's jurisdiction and should have taken place during an open meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Release to the public, within 30 days of receipt of the determination, all e-mails and memoranda referenced in the letter
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law. We also order that the Board release to the public, within 30 days following its receipt of this determination, all e-mails and memoranda referenced in this letter.
